Note::remove¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove(std::string_view needle) const

Delete The First Occurrence Of A Literal Substring¶

remove(needle) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with the first occurrence of the literal string needle deleted from each cell. It is the first-only sibling of remove_all, and the delete-form of replace_first (replace_first(needle, "")).

Use it when a marker is expected once — a leading tag that survived an earlier step, one delimiter you want gone, a single boilerplate fragment. The match is literal (no regex, no case folding); only the leftmost match is removed, and the bytes around it are not otherwise touched, so a mid-string removal can leave a double space.

A cell that does not contain needle is copied through unchanged. The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Only The First Match Goes¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"alpha beta beta", "beta", "none"}).remove("beta"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["alpha  beta", "", "none"]

The first beta in cell 0 is deleted (leaving two spaces); the second remains. "none" has no match and is unchanged.

Example 2: Contrast With remove_all¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"a-b-c"}).remove("-");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["ab-c"]

Only the first - is removed; remove_all("-") would give "abc".

See Also¶

  • Note::remove_all: delete every occurrence.

  • Note::replace_first: the general form — substitute instead of delete.

  • Note::remove_prefix / Note::remove_suffix: delete at a boundary only.
